lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your company announces: "We're changing the team structure."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And suddenly… the project you complained about for six months… is now "my project."

lines.speaker: manager
lines.text: Would you be okay handing this project to Sarah?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Actually… I think there are some risks.

lines.speaker: manager
lines.text: Didn't you say this project was a nightmare?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Sarah wants to change the dashboard?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Why? Because once something becomes ours… we tend to value it more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Our project. Our process. Our spreadsheet. Even our terrible old workflow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Psychologists call this the: Endowment Effect.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We don't just evaluate things based on what they're worth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We also value them differently… because we own them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's why replacing your team's old system can feel like: "We're improving the business."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But replacing your system feels like: "They're destroying everything I've built."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sometimes… the hardest thing to let go of isn't a bad idea.
